transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-08
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Liu (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Vazquez (Polaris ML), Marcus Reed (Infra), Priya Nair (CTO)

[00:00] Jamie (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to cover model selection today — open models, context length, and deployment options, make sure we understand your constraints.
[00:12] Elena (Polaris): yeah thanks jamie. i'll keep it high level — our product is a customer-facing assistant integrated into finance workflows, needs to reference long docs and be bilingual (english/spanish) and eventually support french and japanese.
[00:25] Priya (Polaris): hi all, we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private because we have PII in some documents; ideally VPC or dedicated pool for production.
[00:34] Samir (Redwood): got it, thanks. quick qual — what's your target latency and qps? and typical prompt+context size?
[00:42] Marcus (Polaris): target p50 latency around 250-350ms for short queries; but when we do long-doc summarization it can be higher. typical retrieval windows are 10k–32k tokens depending on how much doc we attach. QPS initially is low, like 5–20 qps, but could spike during batch jobs.
[01:00] Jamie (Redwood): okay that helps. so two use cases: short interactive queries with tight latency SLAs and long-context summarization where cost matters. for model candidates are you leaning open models or commercial blackbox?
[01:12] Elena (Polaris): we prefer open models for cost and control, but we also want the option to fall back to hosted models if quality or latency is an issue. open to Llama 3 variants, mistral, mpt, and any recommended quantized builds.
[01:25] Samir (Redwood): note that Redwood Dedicated and Private can run optimized quantized runtimes; and our hosted offering also provides curated open models with performance profiles. slight transcription note: sometimes the auto notes say 'K-V cash' instead of KV cache haha.
[01:38] Priya (Polaris): yep the KV cache spelling aside, important thing is the model supports efficient kv caching for sessions and long-context A|B. also tool-calling — we need function/tool calling for retrieval and a connector to our vector DB.
[01:52] Jamie (Redwood): good call. Samir, can you speak to tool-calling and function support across models?
[01:56] Samir (Redwood): sure. function-calling depends on model and runtime — many of the open LLMs support structured output prompting but tool-calling (like the OpenAI-style function call) we emulate in the Redwood runtime; we provide deterministic function call hooks and we can wire connectors to your vector DB or REST backends. for dedicated/private we can run custom connectors inside VPC for data residency.
[02:20] Elena (Polaris): what about context length? we need 32k at minimum for some flows. how stable is that across model families and quantized variants?
[02:30] Samir (Redwood): we have two levers: model architecture (some families have native 32k windows) and runtime chunking + prefix caching. For Llama 3 70B variants we can get extended context with sliding window optimizations; Mistral and certain MPT forks also offer 32k variants. important caveat: quantization sometimes reduces peak quality on nuanced multilingual cases. we'll want to benchmark.
[02:55] Marcus (Polaris): multilingual quality is key. english/spanish is our highest volume; we also need decent japanese and french for support docs. do you have per-model multilingual benchmarks?
[03:05] Jamie (Redwood): yes we curate performance profiles — rough guideline: some open models excel in english but drop in accuracy for spanish/japanese. Redwood Optimize can recommend model+quantization choices by workload; but again we'll run your sample prompts to get real numbers.
[03:20] Priya (Polaris): security — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. can Redwood do customer-managed KMS or HSM in private?
[03:32] Samir (Redwood): yes. Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; Dedicated offers VPC peering and audit logs. Hosted can meet SOC2 controls but if you require customer-managed keys or strict egress controls, Private or Dedicated is the way to go.
[03:48] Elena (Polaris): what about data retention and logs? we can't have raw PII stored — need redaction or retention policies.
[03:55] Jamie (Redwood): we offer configurable retention policies and can deploy in a private mode with zero retention on the hosted control plane for certain routes; we'll include the retention options in the security pack.
[04:07] Marcus (Polaris): pricing — rough ballpark for 32k context ops?
[04:12] Jamie (Redwood): pricing varies by model and deployment. for hosted curated open models it's per-token with discounts on committed Dedicated capacity. for 32k contexts the per-response token cost is higher obviously; we'll send sample billing scenarios for your expected qps.
[04:26] Samir (Redwood): also worth mentioning batching and KV caching — for interactive flows caching prefixes can dramatically reduce cost, especially if users request followups. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/caching policies.
[04:40] Elena (Polaris): ideal pilot: run same benchmark across 3 model families (Llama variant, Mistral, MPT), measure p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k requests, and multilingual accuracy on our prompt set. can you do that?
[04:52] Samir (Redwood): yes we can. we'll need a sample corpus and expected traffic profile. Marcus, can you share a sanitized dataset and the prompt bank?
[05:00] Marcus (Polaris): yes i'll prepare a smaller 1k prompt set with english/spanish pairs and some long-doc examples, drop it in the shared drive.
[05:09] Jamie (Redwood): great. timeline? we propose a 2-week SE-led benchmark for the pilot, results and decision meeting after that.
[05:17] Priya (Polaris): 2 weeks sounds good. what's the process for Dedicated capacity if we want to go that route after pilot?
[05:23] Jamie (Redwood): Dedicated is usually a reserved capacity contract (monthly/annual). you can start with hosted pilot and move to dedicated with capacity sizing based on benchmark. Dedicated gives you predictability, isolation, and better latency SLAs. Private on-prem is a separate enterprise agreement with deployment planning.
[05:40] Elena (Polaris): any red flags we should know about, like certain quantized builds breaking multilang?
[05:46] Samir (Redwood): main tradeoff: higher quantization reduces cost but can harm subtle multilingual outputs. also very long context with some models may require runtime stitching which affects latency. we'll spell out the tradeoffs in the benchmark plan.
[05:59] Marcus (Polaris): connectors — we use a vector DB (we'll share the type) and also want ability to call internal APIs for account lookups. can the tool-calling hook be proxied inside our VPC?
[06:10] Samir (Redwood): yes for Dedicated/Private we can run connectors inside your network or via secure tunnels; for hosted we offer secure connector patterns but if you need zero data egress, Private is recommended.
[06:24] Priya (Polaris): ok, last one — rollouts and model pinning. we want canary on new model versions.
[06:30] Jamie (Redwood): Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback policies. you can pin routes to model versions or route by policy (latency vs cost).
[06:42] Elena (Polaris): great. sounds like next steps are shared dataset, security pack, and benchmark plan.
[06:48] Jamie (Redwood): yep. i'll follow up with a formal pilot proposal and pricing. Samir will own the benchmark plan. Marcus you'll send the prompt bank.
[06:58] Priya (Polaris): thanks all, looking forward.
[07:02] Jamie (Redwood): thanks everyone. we'll send docs and set up the SE deep dive workshop.
